title: Simultaneous finite-stage lifting of distinguished triangles and finite equations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the pair category $\mathcal P_T$ and finite-stage categories $\mathcal C_E(T)$ of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], the shift of [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], and the distinguished triangles of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. Equip each $\mathcal C_E(T)$ with the triangulated structure [def-weil-triangulated-category] in which [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] chooses its cone triangles, namely the scalar-localization structure of [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated] (a triangle is distinguished when it is isomorphic to the image of a distinguished triangle of the integral category $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ whose raw scalar localization is $\mathcal C_E(T)$ by [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]), and the transition functors with their exact structures and coherent comparisons $\sigma$ of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

Give finitely many objects $X=(E_X,K_X)$ of $\mathcal P_T$, finitely many arrows between these objects and specified occurrences of their shifts $[1]$, and finitely many true equations formed from these arrows by composition, identities, zero, addition, negatives, and finitely many applications of $[1]$. Select finitely many triangle rows among this data, each distinguished in $\mathcal P_T$; triangles and their isomorphisms mean [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]. A vertex occurring more than once is a single specified object. Fix also a finite intermediate field $M_0$ of $\Qlb/\mathbf Q_\ell$.

Then there is a finite field $M\supseteq M_0,E_X$ for every specified $X$, and representatives of all the arrows over $M$, such that all the specified equations hold in $\mathcal C_M(T)$, and all the selected triangle rows are distinguished in $\mathcal C_M(T)$. The lift of $X$ is $X_M=T_{M/E_X}K_X$, shared across all its occurrences; the lift of $X[1]$ is identified with $X_M[1]$ by $\sigma_{M/E_X,K_X}$. In particular a row $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow iZ\xrightarrow pX[1]$ lifts to
$$X_M\xrightarrow{f_M}Y_M\xrightarrow{i_M}Z_M\xrightarrow{\sigma_{M/E_X,K_X}\circ p_M}X_M[1],$$
where $p_M$ denotes its representative with target $T_{M/E_X}(K_X[1])$. A shifted arrow is the shift of its lifted arrow under these identifications. For repeated shifts use the iterated $\sigma$ comparisons. The common-stage images recover the specified arrows and triangle rows through the vertex isomorphisms $X\xrightarrow{\sim}(M,X_M)$ represented over $M$ by $\operatorname{id}_{X_M}$.

source.place: TR2, TR3 and TR4 common-stage-representation sentences; implicit simultaneous lifting of distinguished rows, their witness isomorphisms and finitely many equations. This is an agent-extracted auxiliary assertion, not a theorem asserted by a Stacks tag.

proof.text: For each selected row $R=(X,Y,Z,f,i,p)$ choose a witnessing common-stage cone triangle $Q$ and an isomorphism $e:Q\to R$, using [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. If the defining witness has the opposite orientation, take its inverse. By [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift], this consists of three component arrows $a,b,c$ and their inverse arrows, with six inverse identities and the three equations $bf_Q=fa$, $ci_Q=ib$, $a[1]p_Q=pc$. Add these objects, arrows, inverses and equations to the original finite data, together with the specified representatives of the arrows of each witness cone triangle at its defining field. Only finitely many data have been added. No axiom for distinguished triangles in $\mathcal P_T$ has been used: the witnesses exist by its definition of distinguishedness.

source.place: TR2--TR4 common-stage-representation sentences; expanded witness argument, step 1

proof.text: Choose representatives for all remaining arrows of this enlarged finite configuration. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], each representative is a map at a finite overfield of its endpoint fields. Take the compositum $L$ of their finitely many fields, all witness fields, all vertex fields and $M_0$. The directedness stated in that definition makes $L$ a finite intermediate extension. Transport each chosen representative by $u_L=a_{L,N,E_Y}T_{L/N}(u)a_{L,N,E_X}^{-1}$. Thus each vertex has the single lift $X_L=T_{L/E_X}K_X$, also when it occurs in multiple rows. This procedure retains the chosen cone representatives rather than choosing unrelated representatives for their arrow classes.

source.place: TR2--TR4 common-stage-representation sentences; expanded witness argument, step 2

proof.text: Expressions in the finite data have compatible stage representatives. For identities, composition and addition this is the common-stage operation formula and additive transport in [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]; zero and negatives follow by additivity. For a shifted map, its representative is $\sigma_Y^{-1}u[1]\sigma_X$. Identifying its source and target by $\sigma_X,\sigma_Y$ gives exactly $u[1]$, since $\sigma_Y(\sigma_Y^{-1}u[1]\sigma_X)\sigma_X^{-1}=u[1]$. Repeat this calculation for the finitely many nested shifts and use the associator compatibility of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Structural induction on each expression now gives a representative for both sides of every prescribed equation. Each equality of their classes holds after some further field by the eventual-equality clause of the calculus. Take a common overfield $M$ for these finitely many equality witnesses and $L$. Transitivity of transport preserves all those equalities at $M$, including the witness inverse identities and the three triangle equations.

source.place: TR2--TR4 common-stage-representation sentences; expanded witness argument, step 3

proof.text:
A witness cone triangle chosen at $N\subseteq M$ is distinguished at $N$ in the triangulated structure specified in the hypotheses. By exactness in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] and [def-weil-triangulated-category], applying $T_{M/N}$ gives a distinguished triangle whose last arrow is $\sigma_{M/N,U}T_{M/N}(p_Q^{\mathrm{stage}})$, where $U=T_{N/E_X}K_X$. Identify its first two vertices with $T_{M/E_X}K_X,T_{M/E_Y}K_Y$ using the associators; its third vertex is $T_{M/N}C$. The first two arrows are the transports from Step 2. For the last arrow the formula in [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] starts with $\sigma_{N/E_X,K_X}^{-1}p_Q^{\mathrm{stage}}$. Compatibility of $\sigma$ with the associators gives
$$\sigma_{M/E_X,K_X}\,a_{M,N,E_X,K_X[1]}\,T_{M/N}(\sigma_{N/E_X,K_X}^{-1}p_Q^{\mathrm{stage}})=a_{M,N,E_X,K_X}[1]\,\sigma_{M/N,U}\,T_{M/N}(p_Q^{\mathrm{stage}}).$$
Thus the corrected transported witness row is isomorphic to that distinguished triangle, so is distinguished by finite-stage TR1. This uses the prescribed finite-stage structures, not a triangulation of the pair category.

source.place: TR2--TR4 common-stage-representation sentences; expanded witness argument, step 4

proof.text:
The lifted $a_M,b_M,c_M$ for $e:Q\to R$ are isomorphisms: their chosen inverse representatives satisfy both inverse identities at $M$ by Step 3. The first two triangle equations hold there too. For the third, write $v_Q,v_R$ for the raw representatives of $p_Q,p$ with targets $T_{M/E_{Q_1}}(K_{Q_1}[1])$ and $T_{M/E_X}(K_X[1])$. Step 3 gives
$$(\sigma_X^{-1}a_M[1]\sigma_{Q_1})v_Q=v_Rc_M.$$
Multiplication by $\sigma_X$ changes this to
$$a_M[1](\sigma_{Q_1}v_Q)=(\sigma_Xv_R)c_M.$$
These are exactly the corrected last arrows of the two stage rows. By [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift] the three components therefore form an isomorphism of those triangles. The corrected witness row is distinguished by Step 4, so finite-stage TR1 in [def-weil-triangulated-category] makes the corrected row $R_M$ distinguished. The same $M$ works for every selected row.

source.place: TR2--TR4 common-stage-representation sentences; expanded witness argument, step 5

proof.text: For $X=(E_X,K_X)$ the arrows $\rho_X:X\to(M,X_M)$ and $\rho_X^{-1}$ represented at $M$ by $\mathrm{id}_{X_M}$ compose to the identity by [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. For any represented $u:X\to Y$, both $\rho_Yu$ and $j_M(u_M)\rho_X$ have representative $u_M$. The shift formula of [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] gives $\rho_X[1]=j_M(\sigma_X)\rho_{X[1]}$, using the normalized identity transition and its compatible shift comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Hence the last-arrow equation for recovery of a row is $\rho_X[1]p=j_M(\sigma_Xp_M)\rho_Z$. Equivalently its image is the raw representative $p_M$, because the common-stage cone formula multiplies the corrected arrow by $\sigma_X^{-1}$. Composition, addition and the calculation in Step 3 recover all equations and all iterated shifted arrows. The same lift $X_M$ is used at every occurrence and $M\supseteq M_0$, as required.
